title: Pilot Decision Frame and One‑Page Ask for Enterprise Inference
author: Aisha Rahman
body:
Purpose

This page is a compact decision frame and one‑page ask designed for field reps and platform advocates running enterprise inference pilots. It bundles concise positioning, a short competitive snapshot, three scaled pricing scenarios, a one‑page slide / email template for the CTO/Platform owner, and a security FAQ tailored for procurement/CISO reviewers. Use this when you have a pilot signal and need an executive‑level yes/no within 2–4 weeks.

Audience
- Sales engineers and account executives handling enterprise pilots
- Solutions architects and platform advocates
- Customer security and procurement teams

TL;DR (elevator scripts)
- For CTO / Platform Owner (15–30 seconds): "Redwood gives you production‑grade LLM inference across hosted and private deployments with predictable per‑token economics and SLA‑backed throughput. We run pilots on your workload profile, measure latency/cost/quality tradeoffs, and deliver a migration plan that preserves model fidelity while cutting inferred unit costs via batching and KV caching."
- For CISO (20–40 seconds): "Pilot data stays isolated; we offer VPC/private deployments or Dedicated capacity with KMS integration, comprehensive audit logs, and documented SOC2 controls. We keep model outputs auditable and can run in your cloud region or on‑prem for regulated use cases."

One‑Page Ask (what to ask the customer for the pilot)
1) Objective: Validate production performance and unit economics for X use case (e.g., multi‑turn chat support for 20k MAU, 99th‑percentile latency target < 250 ms).
2) Success criteria (quantitative):
   - Latency: p99 end‑to‑end < 250 ms for 95% of requests
   - Cost: token cost per interaction ≤ $0.003 (post‑batching/quantization suggestions)
   - Quality: BLEU/ROUGE/LLM‑eval benchmark delta ≤ 3% vs baseline model
   - Reliability: 99.5% API availability during pilot windows
3) Commitment we request from customer:
   - 4–6 weeks of access to real or replayed traffic (or representative synthetic workload)
   - One technical point‑of‑contact and weekly working session (1 hour)
   - Approval for limited production pilot with a canary route (≤ 5% of traffic)

Pilot Delivery Plan (weeks)
1) Week 0 (Prep): onboarding, credentials, security review, sample payloads, test account provisioning.
2) Week 1 (Baseline): run initial profile against hosted catalog models, collect latency/cost/quality metrics.
3) Week 2 (Optimize): apply batching, KV caching, and suggest quantization profile; rerun benchmarks.
4) Week 3 (Canary): route 1–5% traffic to pilot endpoint, monitor SLOs and cost.
5) Week 4 (Wrap & Recommend): deliver pilot report, model variant recommendation, rollout/rollback plan, and pricing proposal.

Competitive snapshot (2‑column brief)
| Competitor | Primary tradeoffs and our positioning |
|---|---:|
| Managed cloud vendor | Strength: deep cloud integrations; Weakness: opaque per‑token economics and limited model variety. 
Positioning: Offer transparent, workload‑level costing and model catalog with verified performance profiles. |
| Self‑hosted runtimes | Strength: control over infra; Weakness: heavy ops burden and slow upgrade cycles. 
Positioning: Provide private deployment options plus a managed control plane and ops playbook to reduce engineering lift. |
| LLM API provider (simplicity) | Strength: easy to start; Weakness: poor latency predictability at scale. 
Positioning: Demonstrate predictable p99 latency with Dedicated and autoscale profiles. |

Pricing scenarios (example constructs for quoting to technical buyer)
Note: these are sample anchor scenarios to quickly convert pilots. Numbers are placeholders; run the pricing simulator prior to quoting.

| Scenario | Ideal for | Commitment | Example economics (hosted) | Add‑ons / Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rapid Eval | Small proof‑of‑concept, minimal infra | 0 $ commit, short term | $0.12 / 1k tokens gen; $0.06 / 1k tokens ctx | 2 weeks priority onboarding |
| Performance Pilot | Validate SLA & p99 latency | 1 mo commitment, dev + test quotas | $0.10 / 1k tokens gen; $0.05 / 1k tokens ctx; tiered discounts after 1M tokens | Includes tuning session and batching config |
| Dedicated Pilot (recommended for scale) | Enterprise with production SLA needs | 3–6 month reserved capacity | Custom per‑hour GPU reserve + blended token pricing; sample: $8k/mo reserve for 1x V100 equiv + $0.035 / 1k tokens | Comes with SLA, private control plane option and audit logs |

Quick pitch deck one‑pager (copyable email or slide)
Subject: Pilot proposal — measurable latency, cost, and quality for [Customer]’s [Use Case]
Body / Slide bullets:
- Problem: unpredictable latency and exploding token costs blocking production LLM adoption
- Redwood value: predictable p99 latency, workload‑aware batching, private deployment options, and straightforward economics
- Ask: 4‑week pilot, sample workload or traffic replay, weekly syncs — we deliver a pilot report and rollout plan
- Quick timeline: onboard (week 0) → baseline (week 1) → optimize (week 2) → canary (week 3) → wrap (week 4)
- Primary success metric: p99 < 250 ms & < $X per interaction

Security & Procurement FAQ (targeted answers for typical concerns)
Q: Where does customer data live during a hosted pilot?
A: For hosted pilots we segregate customer data per‑tenant, store payloads in encrypted buckets in our cloud region, and retain only the minimum telemetry needed for observability. For regulated customers we recommend Redwood Dedicated or Private with VPC peering.

Q: Do you support KMS/HSM and customer key rotation?
A: Yes. Dedicated and Private support KMS integrations (AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault). Customer keys can be rotated on a schedule and we support envelope encryption for model artifacts in transit and at rest.

Q: What audit logs are available?
A: Tokenized request logs, model version, route, request/response latency, and admin actions are logged. Logs can be exported to the customer SIEM (S3, GCS, or streaming to Splunk/Datadog).

Q: Can we run on‑prem in an air‑gapped environment?
A: Yes — we provide an on‑prem package for air‑gapped deployments that includes a private control plane and an ops runbook. On‑prem pilots are handled by the Private deployment team.

Q: How are model changes and rollouts controlled?
A: Rollouts are policy driven: canary %, A/B, auto‑rollback thresholds based on latency, error rate, and quality metrics. We keep immutable model versioning for traceability.

Operational guardrails to propose in the pilot
- SLOs: p99 latency & availability with clear alert thresholds (latency alert at p99 > 300 ms; availability alert at < 99.5%)
- Rate limits: soft quota at pilot ramp to avoid noisy neighbor effects; typically start at 1 RPS per 100 users and ramp to target
- Circuit breakers: automatic fallback to smaller model variant or queued mode when GPU saturation > 85%

Next steps for field (checklist)
1) Confirm scope and success metric with customer (use One‑Page Ask).
2) Select deployment mode: Hosted trial vs Dedicated vs Private.
3) Run security questionnaire; route to Priya if Dedicated/Private is requested.
4) Schedule week 0 kickoff and provide credentials for test account.
